newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares seen rallying on policy hopes.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares seen rallying on policy hopes.

text.p: The prospect that the government will introduce a confidence-boosting policy package later this month is expected to further help Indian stocks extend their rally this week, brokers said at the weekend.
"It is apparent that the government is really concerned about the state of the markets...sentiments have changed," said Ajit Ambani, member-broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).

A blistering rally by blue-chips on New Year's Day pushed up the benchmark Bombay stocks index nearly six percent after the government said it would announce in mid-January a policy package to boost industrial growth and revive sagging capital markets.
"People are more optimistic...a lot of hope is being pinned on government announcements," said Neeraj Roy, head of institutional sales at Prime Broking, a domestic firm.

At the end of a five-hour meeting between Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and industrialists and economists on Tuesday, the government said it was likely to announce a series of policy measures by January 15.
The topics discussed between officials and industrialists included the revival of the capital market, bank credit availability, corporate taxation, delicensing and more opening up of the economy.

The BSE's top 30-share index ended on Friday with an impressive gain in the first week of trading after the Christmas vacation. It surged 178.80 points, or 5.79 percent, to 3,264.06 from the previous week's close of 3,085.20 on December 24.
Indian industry has frequently complained that Deve Gowda's 13-party coalition government has done little to help depressed bourses and ease concerns about a slow-down in the economy.
The Congress party on Friday named Sitaram Kesri to replace former premier P.V. Narasimha Rao as leader of the party's parliamentary party ending weeks of intense speculation.
Analysts said the market had largely discounted the election of a new chief, but fears of political uncertainty lingered.
Congress is the main backer of the ruling United Front's minority coalition.
Some traders said front-running by speculators in pivotal stocks in anticipation of increased fund allocation by foreign institutional investors in Indian markets helped the recent rally.
"Expectations of buying in front-bencher stocks has pepped up market sentiment," one dealer at a foreign brokerage said.
Repeated statements by the government stressing the importance of a buoyant market had improved the confidence of operators and investors, said K.R. Choksey, a top BSE member-broker.
Participants said the bullish trend in the markets was accompanied by a price surge in small-cap stocks indicating broad strength in the current rally.
"After a long time the broader market is also taking part in the rally...people are slowly gaining confidence," Choksey said.
